claim: Each drum gives three flat panels with about 1.26 m2 of sheet
law: Panels = mid-wall circumference x body length left after the chime rings and hoop strips are cut out (0.70 x 1.80 m); it must be less than the whole body between the chimes; the independent review found the README's three sheets of 460 x 1,830 mm per drum (2.5 m2) cannot come from one drum, and the README is corrected

claim: A drum full of water weighs about 240 kg, so it is filled and drained on its stand and never lifted
law: Mass = water volume (pi r2 L) x 1,000 kg/m3 + empty drum

claim: A full drum drains through its 2 in bung in about 2.3 min
law: Torricelli outflow Q = Cd a sqrt(2 g h), Cd 0.6, integrated over the falling level of a horizontal cylinder to the bung centre (the CAL adds the slow tail to the lip); the top bung is open as the vent

claim: A water fill and drain, then a pumped LEL reading below 5 % LEL at both bungs, makes a drum that held a non-volatile oil safe to cut cold
law: 29 CFR 1926.352(i): containers that held flammable substances are filled with water or cleaned, ventilated and tested before cutting; 29 CFR 1910.252(a)(3); hot work barred at or above 10 % of the LEL (29 CFR 1915.14(b)); AWS F4.1:2017 water cleaning
check: Pass level 5 % LEL is half the 10 % hot-work limit; the oils accepted have flash points above 60 C (GHS category 3 upper bound), so little vapour forms at workshop temperatures; the reading, not the purge, is the safeguard. The independent review found that a catalytic sensor calibrated on methane under-reads heavy hydrocarbon vapour (relative response about 0.3 to 0.5), so a true 10 to 15 % LEL could read 5 %: fixed by specifying the LEL channel calibrated on pentane or set with the maker's correction factor (BOM line 4, PR-002)

claim: The end cutter takes a 1.5 mm head out with a crank force of at most 27 N
law: Wheel shear F = tau t2 / (2 tan theta) against the chime wall, feed resistance F tan(theta / 2), 30 % roller losses, 150 mm crank

claim: Two ring cuts at once on a 1.5 mm wall need at most 136 N at the shear head crank
law: Rotary shear F = tau t2 / (2 tan theta), 1.0 mm overlap; edge spreading round the web 100 N at 1.2 mm (estimate, cubic in t); 20 % bearing losses; 2.33 to 1 drive, chains 95 % each; 155 mm crank (CAL section 4)
closed_by: DMP-CAL-001 [D15r]; the spreading force is to measure on a scrap drum at TRL 4

claim: The lever notching punch cuts the five-layer chime notch with at most 131 N on its 500 mm ratchet lever
law: Inclined-edge shear per edge 0.5 tau t2 / tan(rake), rake 10 deg, five layers, 20 % stripping; Tr24 x 5 screw, friction 0.15 (CAL section 9); a flat punch would need about 177 kN, so the rake does the work
closed_by: DMP-CAL-001 [K3]; the chime notch force is the least certain number, to confirm on a scrap chime at TRL 4

claim: The shear head frame and shafts carry the separating force at 1.5 mm with a large margin
law: Web in bending and tension, 25 mm shaft in bending at 1,429 N (CAL section 4); S275 yield 275 MPa, used at 0.6 of yield

claim: The bending roll setting that leaves a panel flat (9.3 to 19.3 mm above the lower roll) lies inside the 60 mm slot travel
law: Elastic and perfectly plastic reverse bending: x - M(x)/Me = k0 / ke, Me = sy b t2 / 6, springback to flat; yield 200 to 300 MPa, wall 0.8 to 1.2 mm (CAL section 5.2)

claim: With the first panel of every drum checked and the dial trimmed, the slip roll leaves panels flat within 10 mm over 1 m
law: Setting allowance 0.29 mm from the derivative of the residual curvature (CAL section 5.3); a change of only 0.02 mm of wall or 5 MPa of yield uses it up, so a setting found once per batch (as first claimed) does not hold from drum to drum (independent review, recomputed in CAL section 5.3): fixed by a straightedge check of the first panel of every drum, a dial trim, and a second pass, turned over if over-bent, for a panel out of tolerance; the dial resolution must be at most a quarter of the allowance
closed_by: DMP-DEC-001 fix F1; DMP-CAL-001 sections 5.3 and 8

claim: Cutting the hoop strips out keeps the slip roll to plain sheet; rolled flat, a hoop crown would stretch about 8.5 %
law: Crown strain = hoop height x change of curvature, against the 0.35 % surface strain of a plain panel in the slip roll: a strain more than ten times larger cannot be put in evenly by three rolls, so a rolled hoop would leave the panel buckled (DMP-DDR-002, P7); a design rationale: the check shows the crown strain is above ten times the panel strain

claim: The geared pinch rolls grip three panels with enough force to drive them through the bend
law: Pinch force needed = 1.5 x feed resistance / (2 x friction 0.15) at the worst steel (300 MPa, 1.2 mm); two M16 screws set 2 kN (CAL section 5.5)

claim: The single driven shear disc pulls the head along the cut at 1.5 mm wall
law: Traction 0.3 x separating force (the edge bites) against the feed resistance (CAL section 4); below 1 the operator pushes the trolley
check: 1.17 of the resistance >= 1 of the resistance
closed_by: DMP-CAL-001 [D15t]; friction 0.3 is a screening value, the fallback is a hand push on the trolley

claim: Every piece one person lifts from bench height is 25 kg or less; heavier pieces, and the shear head and ring head lifted to the rail, are two-person lifts
law: ISO 11228-1 reference mass 25 kg, which holds only for ideal lifting; the independent review put the recommended limit for lifting the 23.7 kg shear head up to the rail beam at about 10 kg, so the build plan and PR-011 make both heads two-person lifts; masses from the station model (CAL section 10)

claim: Every crank and lever force in normal use is at or below 150 N
law: Forces from S5 to S7 and the slip roll crank (20 N at 300 mm, CAL section 5.5); 150 N is the requirement PR-006, a conservative screen for a two-hand crank in a standing posture (EN 1005-3 assessment at TRL 4)

claim: Slots made 7 to 8 mm wide and at least 45 mm from the slip roll nip keep fingers out
law: ISO 13857:2019 Table 4: a slot over 6 mm and up to 8 mm needs at least 20 mm to the danger point (CAL section 7); a slot made over 8 mm would need 80 mm, so the slots are toleranced 7 to 8 mm (fix F4, PR-010)

claim: Cold cutting stays cold: slow shearing of 1.5 mm wall does not heat the cut zone toward an oil's autoignition temperature
law: Plastic work tau t x t per metre plus feed work 365 J, into a 2 mm wide strip (c = 460 J/kg K) with no heat flow away; the independent review showed this is not a bound, since a narrower shear zone (0.2 to 0.9 mm) gives a higher local rise; the cut moves at about 4 m/min, so heat spreads into the sheet; lubricating oils autoignite above about 250 C (220 K above a 30 C workshop); the safeguard is the vapour reading below 5 % LEL (S4), and no grinder or torch is used
closed_by: DMP-STM-001 S4 (the vapour reading is the safeguard); cut edge temperature to measure at TRL 4

claim: Hardened D2 discs and a hardened cutter wheel shear 0.8 to 1.5 mm low-carbon drum steel without chipping
law: Slitter knives for low-carbon sheet are commonly D2 tool steel hardened to about 58 to 62 HRC (cutting tool supplier practice); the drum steel is about 250 MPa yield
check: Within practice; the discs bought are to the BOM line 10 specification (DMP-DEC-001, to confirm when bought, item 1)

claim: Purge water settles and its oil is skimmed off, so the water can be reused
law: Mineral and vegetable oils are less dense than water (about 850 to 920 kg/m3) and separate by gravity; a biodegradable detergent emulsifies some oil, so the water settles overnight before it is reused; the independent review found that fire-resistant hydraulic fluids (phosphate esters, water glycols, polyalkylene glycols) sink or mix with water: they are excluded at acceptance (fix F5, PR-013)
check: Within known science; disposal of the skimmed oil follows local rules (DMP-REG-001)

claim: The process has no burning step, so it gives off none of the smoke of burning paint and oil residue
law: Open burning of coated and oily scrap releases smoke, soot and products of incomplete combustion; the bench set never heats the steel (PR-001)
check: Removed by design; the paint stays on the panels and is removed later by a separate cold step (DMP-DDR-001, D4)

claim: The bench set removes the chisel blows: its cuts and rolling are continuous, and the only impact step is setting the panel ends with a dead-blow mallet
law: Impact noise comes from blows on sheet steel; continuous rotary shearing and rolling at hand speed make no impacts (CAL section 5.4)
check: Within known science as a mechanism; sound levels are not claimed and are measured at TRL 4

claim: The eccentric bush sets the 1.0 mm disc overlap within its adjustment range
law: A 3 mm eccentric moves the upper shaft over a 6 mm range; the overlap is set and locked (DMP-DDR-002, P4)

claim: A cradle roller shaft carries the drum and a person leaning on it (1 kN) well below yield
law: Simply supported 25 mm shaft, two roller loads (CAL section 6); bright steel taken at S275 yield 275 MPa, used at 0.6 of yield

claim: Two people turn about 2.20 drums an hour into flat panels (PR-007 asks 2.5)
law: Rate = 2 x 60 / hands-on minutes per drum (54.6 min, CAL section 8), with the per-drum flatness check of fix F1; task times are estimates; checks the arithmetic only, the timed trial measures the times

claim: Two drain stands purge drums faster than the cradle and slip roll use them
law: Stand cycle 35.3 min a drum (load, fill 11 min, soak 10 min, drain, tip, check; CAL section 8); the independent review found one stand would limit the set to about 1.7 drums an hour: fixed by a second stand and tray (fix F2, BOM lines 1 and 2)

claim: The 60 mm bending roll bends little enough under its worst load that all three panels see the same setting
law: Simply supported roll over 940 mm under 805 N spread along it; mid-span deflection against half the 0.29 mm setting allowance (CAL section 5.5)

claim: The notching punch C-frame jaws stay well below yield
law: Cantilever jaw root bending at the hoop station (CAL section 9); S355 yield 355 MPa used at 0.6 of yield

claim: The rail beam keeps the shear head on a straight line with both heads on it
law: Mid-span deflection of the 80 x 40 x 3 RHS beam under the trolley, both heads and drive (CAL section 4.1), against the 1 mm straightness of PR-004's rail

claim: Option B: one person cuts 1.5 mm drum steel with the 1,050 mm shear lever
law: Inclined blade shear 0.5 tau t2 / tan(rake), rake 8 deg: 2.31 kN; lever and link advantage 22.3, efficiency 0.85; lever throatless shears of this class are sold for 14 gauge (1.9 mm) mild steel (Beverly B-1)

claim: Option B: a 15 t hand-pumped cylinder stretches the widest, thickest panel 2 % past yield
law: F = flow stress x area; 300 MPa yield x 1.1 for strain hardening at 2 %, 234 x 1.2 mm

claim: Option B: a 2 % stretch takes out the drum's curl
law: Stretcher levelling: once the whole section yields in tension the bending stresses that hold the curl are wiped out; needs total strain above curl strain t / 2R (0.21 %) plus yield strain (0.15 %); levellers use 1 to 3 %

claim: Option B: the hand pump handle needs at most 150 N at the stretch force
law: Pressure = force / plunger area (52 mm): 44 MPa; pump piston 8 mm, handle ratio 25, pump efficiency 0.8 (to confirm on the pump bought)

claim: Option B: the two UPN 100 bed channels carry the stretch force in compression
law: Axial stress = F / (2 x 1,350 mm2), ties at 550 to 650 mm keep the channels short against buckling; S275 used at 0.6 of yield

claim: Option B: the wedge grips tighten as the panel pulls
law: A wedge grip holds when the face friction on the panel (serrated, taken as 0.3) exceeds tan(wedge angle) plus the friction on its greased back (0.1); the first check (tan(angle) below 0.3, self-locking) was the wrong criterion (independent review), so the wedge angle is 7 deg; the panel's net section at the serrations is to check if B is chosen

claim: Option B: each panel loses its gripped ends
law: Panel length after stretching = 1,800 - 2 x 60 mm grip + 2 % (PR-012 asks about 1,800 mm)

claim: Option B: two people turn about 1.65 drums an hour into flat panels
law: 15.1 m of cut at a 40 mm bite and 5 s a stroke (377 strokes), plus purge 14, loading 2, handling 6, three stretches of 4 min, ends 3 and deburring 4.4 min
